reflections.title: Our Longing for a True Priest

reflect.text: In this story, Micah hired a young Levite to serve as his personal priest. Human beings have always longed for a priest. Deep down, people know God exists, but they also feel their own wrongdoing and know they are unworthy to come near to Him. Throughout history, people have sought someone to stand between them and God, hoping that person could speak for them and offer acceptable worship.

We need to beware of any kind of religion that ignores this deep craving. Some systems try to reduce faith to mere high thoughts or moral ideas. Those ideas fail because they do not take away human sin or provide a lasting foundation for peace. Micah recognized his need for a priest, but he tried to meet it through his own money, a hired man, and handmade images.

Every human priest must ultimately fail to satisfy our need. As F. B. Meyer observed, "stars are needless when the sun has arisen." God has set aside all earthly priests by giving us Jesus Christ as our great High Priest in heaven. Because Jesus represents us before God, we no longer need human go-betweens to secure God's favor.

questions: In what ways might we be tempted to trust in human religious leaders instead of relying on Jesus?
How does knowing Jesus is your High Priest give you confidence when you feel unworthy before God?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, thank You for understanding our deep need for someone to bring us to You. We thank You for Jesus Christ, our great High Priest, who has made peace for us. Help us to rest completely in His work rather than our own efforts to win Your favor. Amen.
